You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Hijack followed by finish writes to a hijacked connection. `Hijack` does not set `committed`, so `finish` runs `sendBuffered`/`commit` on the hijacked writer. Reproduced with a real httptest server and captured ErrorLog. Logged: `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection from ...(*etagWriter).commit (etag.go:134)`. With a prior buffered Write, it also logs `http: response.Write on hijacked connection from ...sendBuffered (etag.go:142)`. The If-None-Match path does the same (`commit(304)` after hijack). Fix: set `committed = true` (and `wroteHeader`) in `Hijack` before forwarding, or return early in `finish` when hijacked.
- [blocking] Malformed member with a valid quoted prefix matches. `etagListContains` returns true for `"a"b`, `"a"garbage`, `W/"a"b`, and `"a"x,"zz"` against an ETag of `"a"`. Criterion 6 says malformed members never match. No test covers this case.
- [minor] The new test file has no real-server hijack test, so the defect above is invisible to the suite. `TestETagHijackAndPushForwarded` checks only the fake writer.
- [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is an untracked file at the repo root. It was already present before this review and is not part of the stated diff; it should not be committed with this change.
- [minor] Flush clears the computed ETag (by design per criterion 10), so a response flushed mid-body has no ETag. This matches the spec and is noted only for awareness.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Failed Hijack after a buffered write still commits the response with no computed ETag. Probe: a wrapper whose Hijack returns an error, handler does `Write("body")`, then Hijack, then `Write("!")`. Result: `etag="" code=200 body="body!"`. Cause: `Hijack` calls `sendBuffered` before the underlying Hijack, so the 200 is committed and `finish` returns early. Criterion 2 is not met for this path. This needs a real Hijacker that returns an error, which is rare in net/http, so the orchestrator may choose to downgrade it to minor.
- [minor] Handler bypasses the wrapper with `Unwrap()` and hijacks the raw writer. The real server logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection from ...(*etagWriter).commit (etag.go:153)`. This is the same symptom as finding 1, but only the handler's own bypass reaches it, and compress.go has the same property.
- [minor] Not reproduced: `etagListContains` panics, infinite loops, or quadratic behaviour on 1 MB inputs (repeated quotes, `W/` runs, `"a"x` runs, 300k-member lists).
- [minor] Not reproduced: `"a", *` matches a 200 whose ETag is `"a"`. That is correct, and my probe expectation was wrong.
- [minor] The `*` check uses `strings.TrimSpace`, which also trims Unicode spaces. Header values rarely carry them, so this is a nit.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix round 1 for the new `middleware.ETag` in go-chi/chi (repo /tmp/ff-eval-tkfj0hhz/workspace; files middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go, already written). The reviewer reproduced two blocking findings; fix both, test-first.

1. After a successful Hijack, `finish` still calls WriteHeader/Write on the hijacked writer. A real httptest server logs "http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection" from commit, and "response.Write on hijacked connection" from sendBuffered when bytes were buffered. It also happens on the If-None-Match path. Fix: after a successful Hijack, the middleware must write nothing more, so finish, Flush and Write don't touch the underlying writer. Add a real-server test that captures the server's ErrorLog (httptest.NewUnstartedServer, set Config.ErrorLog to a log.Logger writing into a buffer, Start) and asserts nothing is logged, for three cases: hijack with no writes, hijack after a buffered Write, and hijack with If-None-Match `*`. Close the hijacked conn inside the handler, then wait for the handler to return before checking the log (e.g. a done channel closed via defer in a wrapping handler outside ETag).
2. `etagListContains` matches malformed members that start with a valid quoted tag: `"a"b`, `"a"garbage`, `W/"a"b` and `"a"x,"zz"` all match ETag `"a"`. A member only counts when its closing quote is followed by optional whitespace and then `,` or end of string; otherwise it's malformed and must not match. Keep scanning later members, so `"a"x, "a"` still matches. Also make sure a bare trailing `W/` or `W` without a quote can't index past the end. Add those cases to TestETagIfNoneMatchRules.

FILES: middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go only. Don't touch README.md or FEATURE_FLOW.md.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `middleware.ETag` has signature `func(next http.Handler) http.Handler` with a doc comment describing behavior and the NoCache ordering note.
2. GET or HEAD, handler responds 200 (explicitly or implicitly by just writing / writing nothing) without setting ETag → response carries a strong ETag (`"..."`, no `W/`, only RFC 9110 etagc characters) computed deterministically from the body (e.g. sha256); same body → same ETag, different body → different ETag; body sent unchanged.
   Hostile: handler writes nothing (empty 200 on GET still gets an ETag); body written in many small Writes equals one big Write's ETag; a 5 MB body is delivered intact.
3. HEAD: when the HEAD handler writes the same body as GET (as with GetHead routing HEAD to the GET handler), its ETag equals the GET ETag. When a HEAD handler writes no body bytes, do NOT compute an ETag (omitting beats emitting a wrong one); a handler-set ETag is still used for If-None-Match.
4. Handler-set ETag (strong or weak) is left untouched and used for matching.
5. If-None-Match matches the response ETag on a 200 GET/HEAD → status 304, no body, ETag header kept, Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding removed (as net/http's ServeContent does), other headers (Cache-Control, Vary, etc.) kept.
6. Matching per RFC 9110 §13.1.2 weak comparison: `W/"x"` matches `"x"` either way round; comma-separated lists with optional whitespace; multiple If-None-Match header lines are combined; `*` (as the whole trimmed field value) matches any 200 response.
   Hostile: `"a","b"` no spaces; ` , ,"b" ` empty members; an ETag containing a comma inside quotes (`"a,b"`) must match exactly and must not match `"a"`; malformed members (unquoted `abc`, unterminated `"abc`) never match and never panic; empty If-None-Match → normal 200; `"ABC"` must not match `"abc"` (case-sensitive).
7. Non-GET/HEAD methods (POST, PUT, DELETE…) pass straight through: next receives the original ResponseWriter unwrapped, no ETag added, If-None-Match ignored.
8. Non-200 final statuses (201, 204, 206, 301, 404, 500, …) pass through unchanged: same status, headers, body; no ETag added, no 304 even if If-None-Match matches or is `*`. Once a non-200 status is known, write through without buffering.
9. Writer semantics: second WriteHeader call ignored (first wins); 1xx informational WriteHeader (e.g. 103 with a Link header) is forwarded immediately and doesn't count as the final status; Write before WriteHeader means 200; Write returns (len(p), nil) while buffering.
10. Wrapper capabilities, like compress.go: Flush on a 200 being buffered stops buffering — writes headers (no computed ETag; handler-set one kept) and the buffered bytes to the client, flushes, then streams the rest directly (no 304 possible after that); Hijack and Push forward to the underlying writer or return the compress.go-style errors when unavailable; Unwrap returns the underlying writer so http.NewResponseController works.
11. Tests in middleware/etag_test.go cover every criterion and hostile input above; README has the ETag row and its pkg.go.dev link line.
12. Standing: existing suite passes with -race; `go vet ./...` clean; `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.

CHECKS: while working `go test -race -run ETag ./middleware`; at the end `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./middleware .`.
